distinguishing_feature: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs specifically in the postpartum period independent of active breastfeeding status.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with non-purulent nipple discharge and ductal dilation rather than acute infectious inflammation.
[LLM DRAFT] Characterized by a smooth, fluid-filled mass without signs of acute inflammation, warmth, or fever.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents later in gestation, typically with more pronounced physiologic breast enlargement and glandular development.
[LLM DRAFT] Occurs exclusively post-delivery during breastfeeding rather than during early pregnancy.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a circumscribed, fluid-filled mass without localized signs of acute inflammation, erythema, or systemic infection.
[LLM DRAFT] Occurs during the earlier 1-13 weeks gestational window rather than weeks 14-27.
[LLM DRAFT] Develops during the postpartum breastfeeding period rather than during the ongoing second trimester of gestation.
[LLM DRAFT] General breast and nipple abscess presentation not specifically tied to the hormonal and physiological state of the second trimester of pregnancy.
[LLM DRAFT] Occurs during active breastfeeding rather than the broader postpartum/puerperal period without lactation focus.
[LLM DRAFT] Involves the nipple and areolar complex specifically, often presenting with subareolar duct involvement and fistulae.
[LLM DRAFT] A chronic, non-bacterial inflammatory condition featuring dilated ducts and nipple discharge, rather than an acute localized purulent collection.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with non-cyclic nipple discharge and subareolar inflammation without acute localized purulent collection.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a smooth, mobile, fluid-filled mass lacking the acute local erythema, warmth, and tenderness of an infection.
[LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging, lacking the acute pain, inflammation, and fluctuance of an abscess.

[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a fluid-filled, mobile mass that typically demonstrates benign features on ultrasound rather than the non-palpable microcalcifications or incidental findings characteristic of LCIS.
[LLM DRAFT] Manifests as a rapidly growing cutaneous or subcutaneous nodule originating from the skin rather than the terminal ductulo-lobular unit.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with nipple discharge or periareolar inflammation due to dilated ducts rather than the clonal proliferation of epithelial cells confined to the lobules seen in LCIS.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a well-circumscribed, fluid-filled mass on imaging rather than dilated, fluid-filled subareolar ducts.
[LLM DRAFT] Characterized by acute localized inflammation, severe pain, erythema, and purulent discharge rather than chronic, bland periductal inflammation.
[LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and detected mammographically as microcalcifications rather than presenting with palpable subareolar masses or nipple discharge.
[LLM DRAFT] Arises from the glandular breast tissue rather than the overlying skin and is typically non-invasive and clinically occult.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with acute inflammatory signs such as localized erythema, warmth, tenderness, and purulent discharge rather than a firm, painless cutaneous nodule.
[LLM DRAFT] Characterized by dilated subareolar ducts often leading to nipple retraction or thick discharge rather than a primary dermal malignant neoplasm.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a similar benign, fluid-filled mass but is located in the contralateral breast.
[LLM DRAFT] Manifests as non-invasive neoplastic cellular proliferation rather than a benign fluid-filled cavity.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with acute inflammatory signs such as localized erythema, warmth, and purulent tenderness rather than a smooth, painless cyst.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents identically to a right breast cyst but is located in the contralateral breast.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with nipple discharge and ductal dilation rather than a discrete fluid-filled mass.
[LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and detected on biopsy or mammography rather than presenting as a palpable fluid-filled cyst.
[LLM DRAFT] Laterality specification helps differentiate the exact anatomical location compared to an unspecified breast cyst.
[LLM DRAFT] Laterality specification distinguishes the exact side of the lesion from a cyst with unspecified laterality.
[LLM DRAFT] Histological malignancy rather than a benign fluid-filled cyst distinguishes this neoplastic condition.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a painless, rapidly growing cutaneous nodule rather than an acute physical trauma.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with localized pain, erythema, and purulent discharge rather than acute structural tissue loss from trauma.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents as a fluid-filled, mobile breast mass rather than an acute open structural injury to the chest wall.
